title: The Upside-Down Temple Built for Water
description: Rani ki Vav, the 11th-century stepwell in Patan, Gujarat.

scenes.narration: Most temples reach up to the sky. This one goes down into the earth.
scenes.image_prompt: deep ornate Indian stepwell with carved stone levels descending to water

scenes.narration: It's the 11th century, in Patan, Gujarat. A queen builds a stepwell in memory of her husband, King Bhimdev the First.
scenes.image_prompt: medieval Indian queen in royal attire overlooking a stepwell under construction

scenes.narration: Steps lead down seven levels to the water.
scenes.image_prompt: looking down seven tiers of carved pillared galleries to water at the bottom

scenes.narration: The walls hold hundreds of sculptures of gods, goddesses and celestial dancers.
scenes.image_prompt: close up of intricate stone carvings of Hindu deities and dancers on stepwell walls

scenes.narration: In dry months, people walk down to reach the water and stay cool.
scenes.image_prompt: villagers in traditional clothes carrying brass pots down stepwell stairs

scenes.narration: Over time, floods from the Saraswati river buried it in silt.
scenes.image_prompt: stepwell half buried under mud and silt, overgrown

scenes.narration: That silt protected the carvings for centuries.
scenes.image_prompt: archaeologists brushing silt off perfect stone sculptures

scenes.narration: It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site and appears on the hundred rupee note. Have you seen it?
scenes.image_prompt: Rani ki Vav today in warm afternoon light, wide view
